title: The stranger was the teacher
hookLine: Pukkusati meets the Buddha in a potter's shed without knowing him, and is taught the six elements

cards: Evening, on the road near Rajagaha. A wandering monk asks a potter named Bhaggava if he can spend the night in his workshop. The potter says: fine by me, but someone's already staying there.
Ask him. Inside is a man who has left home for the homeless life out of faith in a teacher he has never met. His name is Pukkusati.
The traveler asks: may I stay? Pukkusati says: the workshop is roomy. Stay as you like.
He has no idea who just walked in.

teach.b: They sit through most of the night. Then the traveler asks: on whose account did you go forth? Who's your teacher?
Pukkusati answers: the recluse Gotama, the Sakyan. Have you seen him? Would you recognize him?
No, says Pukkusati. I've never seen him. If I saw him, I wouldn't know him.
The Buddha doesn't reveal himself. He thinks: this young man went forth on my account. Let me teach him.

teach.h: SIX ELEMENTS: NOT MINE, NOT ME
teach.b: A person, he says, is made of six elements: earth, water, fire, air, space and consciousness. The solid in the body is earth, and so is the solid outside it.
Seeing that, you see: this is not mine, this is not me, this is not my self. Same for water, fire, air and space.

Then what remains is consciousness, and then a pure, bright equanimity, like gold refined by a goldsmith until it's soft and shining. Even that, he says, is conditioned, and he shows how to let go of it too.
When the teaching ends, Pukkusati understands who's speaking.
He bows and asks forgiveness for calling the Buddha friend, like an equal. The Buddha accepts. Pukkusati asks for full ordination, and is told he needs a bowl and robes.
He goes to find them, and on the way, the text says, a stray cow kills him. The Buddha tells the monks Pukkusati had already gone far, beyond returning to this world.
He had found his teacher, for one night, without knowing it.

how: The six-element contemplation of MN 140 is taught in Theravada and other meditation traditions, with practitioners reviewing earth, water, fire, air, space and consciousness in the body and seeing each as not-self.

o: a potter's workshop or clay shed
a teacher one has never met in person
an element, like earth, water or fire

games.q: a night in the potter's shed: tap the pairs.
p: the potter who owned the workshop
went forth for a teacher he'd never seen
earth, water, fire, air, space, consciousness

s: Pukkusati recognizes the Buddha the moment he walks in
he says he's never seen him and wouldn't know him; he realizes who it is only when the teaching ends.
the Buddha teaches Pukkusati before revealing who he is
he thinks: this young man went forth on my account; let me teach him.
Pukkusati received full ordination from the Buddha that night
he went to find a bowl and robes, and the text says a stray cow killed him on the way.

games.q: you're the Buddha. a young man in a potter's shed says he went forth because of you, but wouldn't recognize you. what do you do?
o: tell him at once who you are.
teach him, and let him discover it.
games.why: the Buddha teaches him the six elements first; Pukkusati recognizes him through the teaching itself.

practice: Feel the solid in you: earth; the moist: water; the warmth: fire; the breath moving: air; the spaces in mouth and ears: space; and the knowing of it all: consciousness.
Then think of someone you'll meet whom you don't really know, a cashier, a driver, a new colleague, and leave a little room for the possibility that they have something to teach you.

wordCard.voice: Dhatu. Element: Pukkusati spent a night in a potter's shed with the Buddha, not knowing him, and was taught the six elements, or dhatus. Today's word.

orig.note: Pali dhatu: element. MN 140 teaches six: earth, water, fire, air, space and consciousness.

carryVoice: Your line: found his teacher without knowing. A roomy workshop, and a door left open. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Majjhima Nikaya 140, Dhatuvibhanga Sutta (the exposition of the elements)
